absent: Complete Hyper-V CPUID leaf contents beyond the truncated point and enlightenment version negotiation.
Internals of flush, IPI send, signal event, and hypercall completion helpers.
Synthetic-debug enablement and userspace completion protocol details.
Connection-to-event table lookup, teardown, and notification delivery paths.
Protected-APIC interrupt helper and nested event query internals.

findings.text: Main Hyper-V hypercall dispatcher validates guest privilege and CPU mode, decodes control word and guest addresses from registers according to address width, enforces per-code access policy and reserved-bit rules, optionally captures vector registers for eligible fast calls, then routes each code to in-kernel handling, userspace exit, or rejection status with a unified completion path.
Hypercall handling requires supervisor privilege and protected mode; otherwise an undefined-opcode exception is queued and handling ends immediately without further decoding or state change.

Control word decoding separates operation code, variable-header count, fast flag, repeat count and repeat start; a repeat indicator derives from nonzero repeat count or start. Decoded fields plus input and output guest addresses are observed by trace.

Access control is bypassed when enforcement is disabled; otherwise each operation is authorized against cached enlightenment and feature flags, with extended processor-mask operations additionally requiring the extended-mask recommendation, debug operations interacting with synthetic-debug enablement, and extended calls requiring the extended-hypercall feature.

Only flush list and space operations including extended forms plus extended IPI send are eligible for vector-register fast input; when enforcement is on, use of that path without the vector-input feature raises an undefined-opcode exception instead of proceeding.
Vector input capture acquires the floating point unit, reads each architected vector register into descriptor slots, then releases the unit.

After validation, dispatch either completes inline with a status, performs a spin-yield hint, invokes flush or IPI helpers, forwards message or event or debug or extended operations to userspace with exit reason and inputs recorded plus a completion callback armed, or returns invalid-code or invalid-input or access-denied or operation-denied statuses for disallowed combinations.

Spin notification and signal event reject repeat or variable headers; flush list requires a repeat count with zero start; flush space and IPI sends reject any repeat indication and non-extended forms also reject variable headers; debug post and retrieve reject fast mode while reset additionally requires synthetic-debug enablement and hypercall-based option; extended range rejects fast mode.

Observed Hyper-V operation identifiers include spin-wait notification, post message, signal event, debug post retrieve and reset, flush list and space with extended variants, IPI send with extended variant, and an extended-call range from query-capabilities to maximum.
Observed completion statuses include success, access denied, invalid hypercall code, invalid hypercall input, invalid parameter, invalid port identifier, and operation denied.
Userspace hypercall exit uses the Hyper-V exit reason with hypercall subtype, carrying the original control word and both guest addresses, with a dedicated completion callback armed for resumption.
VM-scoped Hyper-V initialization prepares the Hyper-V lock and the connection-to-event notification table.
The Hyper-V lock serializes allocation and removal in the connection-to-event table during eventfd assignment and deassignment.

Hyper-V eventfd control validates flags against the deassign bit and connection identifier against the allowed mask, then dispatches to assign with a file descriptor or to deassign by identifier; assignment on an existing connection maps to an existence error while removal of an unknown connection reports absence.
Removal drops the table entry under lock, waits for read-side grace before releasing the event reference, so concurrent readers cannot observe a freed notification object.

Hyper-V CPUID provider fills a fixed ordered leaf set covering vendor and limits, interface, version, features, enlightenment info, implementation limits, synthetic-debug leaves, and nested features, adjusting enlightenment and feature bits from vCPU state, nested enablement, and host topology.
Caller buffer sizing is contractual: a count smaller than the fixed leaf total fails with too-big indication, while a larger count is clamped to the fixed total before filling.

Spin notification performs best-effort directed yield across online vCPUs using a round-robin start after the last boosted index, skipping the caller and unsuitable targets, recording the successful target, and always clearing spin state before return.
Spinning vCPU marks itself in-spin on entry and clears that mark on exit while also clearing its directed-yield eligibility for the next loop; alternate build configuration makes these marks no-ops.

Candidate targets must be marked ready, must not be blocking unless independently runnable, must satisfy kernel-mode preemption policy accounting for pending interrupts, and must pass directed-yield eligibility which toggles while in-spin when relaxation interception is available.
Directed-yield selection is best-effort and racy under concurrent spinners, so multiple spinners may target the same vCPU and ordering is only approximate.

Yield targeting acquires the target identifier lock in try mode, takes a task reference if present, releases the lock, then yields and drops the reference; absence of lock, identifier, or task results in no yield.

Runnable for yield purposes means architecture-runnable or async-fault work pending; architecture-runnable on this platform means running micro-state without halt, paravirtual unhalted indication, or any pending event.

Pending-event check is a disjunction over async-fault completions, allowed init or SIPI, queued exceptions including triple fault, NMI and optionally SMI and PMI requests or pending state subject to allowance, protected-guest-state updates, maskable interrupts when allowed and present, synthetic-timer pending, nested events in guest mode, and Xen pending events.

Interrupt presence first consults external interrupts, then for protected guests delegates to the protected-APIC helper, otherwise consults LAPIC state; external-interrupt logic depends on kernel versus user LAPIC, Xen upcall state, PIC acceptance derived from LAPIC enable and LVT masking and delivery mode, and kernel IOAPIC versus split-chipset userspace pending vector.
Protected-mode determination reads the protection-enable bit from control register state through a power-of-two-checked bit-test helper.

In-kernel determination for preemption treats protected-guest state as in-kernel and otherwise compares the current privilege level against supervisor level, with a weak default equating preempted-in-kernel to in-kernel and a weak default reporting no pending interrupt for yield.
Per-vCPU spin bookkeeping exposes an in-spin indicator and a directed-yield eligibility indicator updated as a pair during spin handling.

Hypercall descriptor logically carries operation code, variable count, fast flag, repeat count and index plus derived repeat flag, input and output guest addresses, original control word, and vector-register snapshot slots for eligible fast calls.
Exception queuing helper forwards a vector number to the multiple-exception machinery with default error and payload semantics.
